question.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Secant or Cosecant
question.problem: What is the general solution to the equation $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\sqrt{2}?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\text{arcsin}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/269d503189ab1027c3d8028542ef0c6a0e2f146aef0f7916691428866ce1b894.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the given equation is

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{4}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{3\pi }{4}+2n\pi .
$$
